### Decisions

A settled decision is just the rule in the document that owns its scope; do not call it out as a decision or create a separate decision record. A system-wide technical rule belongs in the [system architecture (source: guides/product-documentation-process.md#system-architecture)] document; a rule that spans more than one slice of a feature belongs in that feature's system design (see included section "Feature system design"); and a rule contained in one slice belongs in that slice's [technical design (source: guides/product-documentation-process.md#technical-design-document)]. A product-direction rule belongs in the [product vision (source: guides/product-documentation-process.md#product-vision)], and a rule about one feature's promise belongs in its [Product Requirements Document (source: guides/product-documentation-process.md#feature-product-requirements-document)].

When the reason for a settled rule is not obvious, preserve the reasoning beside it as briefly as possible; use more than one sentence when needed. An open decision is one that needs the developer's input or unfinished research. Put it in the owning document's open decisions and tag it `[NEEDS YOUR CALL]`. When a decision changes, revise the rule in place rather than leaving competing current readings.

Future product ideas that are not ready for a document live in the [roadmap](skill://draft-system-design/references/product-documentation-process--roadmap.md) as ideas, not as decisions.
